market_context: United States and general English-speaking market
title: Fresh vs. canned tomatoes: nutrition differences

seo.title: Fresh vs. canned tomatoes: vitamin C, sodium and lycopene
seo.meta_description: Fresh tomatoes retain more vitamin C; canned tomatoes remain low-calorie and heat processing can improve lycopene bioavailability. Compare equal weights.
seo.search_intent: Compare fresh and canned tomato nutrition

excerpt: A USDA raw tomato reference provides 18 calories, 1.2 g fiber and about 12.7 mg vitamin C per 100 g. Canned tomatoes packed in tomato juice provide about 16 calories, 1.9 g fiber, 2.6 mg vitamin C and 115 mg sodium. Heat can lower vitamin C while making tomato lycopene easier to absorb.
content_html:
Canned tomatoes are not nutritionally empty versions of fresh tomatoes. Processing can reduce heat-sensitive vitamin C while improving access to lycopene.

Equal 100 g comparison

Raw tomatoCanned in tomato juice
Calories1816
Fiber1.2 g1.9 g
Vitamin C~12.7 mg~2.6 mg
Sodium~5 mg~115 mg

Calories barely change. Vitamin C and sodium show much larger differences.

Sodium is a recipe issue

No-salt-added canned tomatoes can be very low in sodium. Regular packs may add salt, so the label matters much more than the fact that the tomato is canned.

Lycopene behaves differently

Human research has found lycopene to be more bioavailable from processed tomato products than from raw tomato. Heat and mechanical disruption help release carotenoids from plant-cell structures, and dietary fat can further aid absorption.

This does not mean heating magically creates lycopene. It changes the food matrix and can make the compound easier for the body to access.

Fresh still has an advantage for vitamin C

Vitamin C is heat-sensitive, so fresh tomatoes generally retain more. A diet can easily obtain vitamin C from many other fruits and vegetables, while canned tomatoes remain a useful source of vegetables, potassium and carotenoids.

Use fresh for texture and raw dishes; canned for sauces, soups and convenience. Nutritionally, the two formats complement each other.

faq.question: Are canned tomatoes higher in calories?
faq.answer: No. The references here are 16 calories/100 g canned versus 18 raw.

faq.question: Which has more vitamin C?
faq.answer: Fresh tomato in this comparison: about 12.7 versus 2.6 mg/100 g.

faq.question: Why can canned tomatoes be higher in sodium?
faq.answer: Salt may be added during processing; no-salt-added products are available.

faq.question: Is lycopene easier to absorb from cooked tomatoes?
faq.answer: Human studies indicate processing and heating can increase lycopene bioavailability.
